message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and to ensure they receive a safe, habitable living environment. Below is a concise overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of the unit’s condition at move‑in and move‑out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition. | • Report problems promptly; document all communications. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord may enter only for repairs, inspections, or emergencies.
• Must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entry notices you receive. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are limited to 10% of the monthly rent. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if needed. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease is required for leases longer than one year.
• Lease must specify rent amount, due date, security deposit, and lease duration. | • Review lease carefully before signing. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if discrimination occurs. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide written notice (30 days for nonpayment, 60 days for lease violations).
• Eviction requires a court order; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | • Respond to notices promptly; seek legal counsel if threatened with eviction. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenants have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report disturbances or harassment. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair major issues, tenant may pay for repairs and deduct cost from rent (subject to limits). | • Keep receipts and follow proper procedure. | | **Subletting** | • Tenants may sublet with landlord’s consent; landlords cannot unreasonably deny consent. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Notice of Termination** | • For month‑to‑month leases, either party must give 30 days’ written notice to terminate. | • Provide written notice in a timely manner. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, receipts, photographs of unit condition, and written communication with your landlord. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code (Chapter 24) and local ordinances that may provide additional protections. 3. **Communicate in Writing** – Whenever possible, send notices and complaints via certified mail or email with read receipts. 4. **Seek Legal Assistance** – If you face eviction, discrimination, or a landlord’s failure to maintain habitability, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local legal aid organization. 5. **File Complaints** – Report violations to the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. --- #### Want a Sample Lease? If you’d like a sample residential lease that incorporates these rights and obligations, let me know the type of lease (e.g., month‑to‑month, fixed‑term) and any specific provisions you need, and I can generate a draft for you.
